---
title: "Does Money Buy Olympic Success?"
subtitle: "Milestone 6 · Exploring World Bank GDP (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD) and Unique Olympic Event Medals (1960–2016)"
author: "Emma Acedo Lapieza"
date: today
---

```{r}
#| label: setup-money-medals

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(countrycode)
library(jsonlite)

# 1. Load the Olympic dataset (1896–2016)
olympics <- read_csv("data/athlete_events.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2. Load real World Bank GDP data (indicator NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, current US$, 1960–2016)
# Fetches directly from the World Bank REST API if the local CSV cache is not present
wb_cache_path <- "data/world_bank_gdp.csv"
if (!file.exists(wb_cache_path)) {
  wb_url <- "https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD?date=1960:2016&format=json&per_page=20000"
  wb_raw <- fromJSON(wb_url)
  wb_gdp <- as_tibble(wb_raw[[2]]) |>
    transmute(
      iso3c = countryiso3code,
      country_wb = country$value,
      Year = as.integer(date),
      gdp_usd = as.numeric(value)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(iso3c), nchar(iso3c) == 3, !is.na(gdp_usd)) |>
    arrange(iso3c, Year)
  write_csv(wb_gdp, wb_cache_path)
} else {
  wb_gdp <- read_csv(wb_cache_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
}

# Define our consistent 12 selected European countries from the rest of the website
euro_nocs <- c(
  "ESP", "GBR", "FRA", "GER", "ITA", "SWE",
  "NOR", "NED", "HUN", "FIN", "SUI", "POL"
)

# Historical, dissolved, or multi-state Olympic NOCs that cannot be mapped 1-to-1
# to a single modern sovereign country's World Bank GDP series
excluded_historical_nocs <- c(
  "URS", # Soviet Union
  "GDR", # East Germany
  "FRG", # West Germany
  "EUN", # Unified Team (1992 post-Soviet republics)
  "TCH", # Czechoslovakia
  "YUG", # Yugoslavia
  "SCG", # Serbia and Montenegro
  "UAR", # United Arab Republic
  "WIF", # West Indies Federation
  "AHO", # Netherlands Antilles
  "IOA", # Individual Olympic Athletes
  "ROT", # Refugee Olympic Team
  "EUA", # United Team of Germany
  "RHO"  # Rhodesia
)

# Build a verified NOC-to-ISO3 lookup table for Olympic years >= 1960
noc_iso_lookup <- olympics |>
  filter(Year >= 1960) |>
  distinct(NOC) |>
  mutate(
    iso3c = case_when(
      NOC %in% excluded_historical_nocs ~ NA_character_,
      NOC == "LIB" ~ "LBN", # Lebanon competed under IOC code LIB through 2016
      NOC == "SIN" ~ "SGP", # Singapore competed under IOC code SIN through 2016
      NOC == "KOS" ~ "XKX", # Kosovo uses XKX in World Bank data
      TRUE ~ countrycode(NOC, origin = "ioc", destination = "iso3c", warn = FALSE)
    )
  )

# Deduplicate team events so each country receives 1 medal per unique event
# Restrict to 1960–2016 (years when World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD data is available)
medals_unique_1960 <- olympics |>
  filter(!is.na(Medal), Year >= 1960) |>
  distinct(Year, Season, Games, Sport, Event, NOC, Medal)

# Count unique event medals by NOC and Summer Olympic year (1960–2016)
# Note: In 1960 and 1964, GER represented the combined United Team of Germany (East + West),
# so we exclude GER in 1960 and 1964 to avoid mismatching a combined team to single-state GDP.
summer_medals_by_noc <- medals_unique_1960 |>
  filter(
    Season == "Summer",
    !(NOC == "GER" & Year %in% c(1960, 1964))
  ) |>
  group_by(Year, Games, NOC) |>
  summarise(
    Total_Medals = n(),
    Gold = sum(Medal == "Gold"),
    Silver = sum(Medal == "Silver"),
    Bronze = sum(Medal == "Bronze"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(noc_iso_lookup, by = "NOC") |>
  filter(!is.na(iso3c)) |>
  inner_join(wb_gdp, by = c("iso3c", "Year")) |>
  mutate(
    GDP_Billions = gdp_usd / 1e9,
    Medals_Per_100B_GDP = round(Total_Medals / (gdp_usd / 1e11), 2),
    Group = case_when(
      NOC == "USA" ~ "United States (USA)",
      NOC == "ESP" ~ "Spain (ESP)",
      NOC %in% euro_nocs ~ "Selected Europe (Other 11 Countries)",
      TRUE ~ "Rest of World"
    ),
    Group = factor(
      Group,
      levels = c(
        "United States (USA)",
        "Spain (ESP)",
        "Selected Europe (Other 11 Countries)",
        "Rest of World"
      )
    ),
    Hover_Text = paste0(
      "<b>", country_wb, "</b> (NOC: ", NOC, " · ISO3: ", iso3c, ")<br>",
      "Olympic Games: <b>", Games, "</b><br>",
      "Region Group: ", Group, "<br>",
      "World Bank GDP: <b>$", formatC(GDP_Billions, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","), " Billion</b><br>",
      "Unique Event Medals: <b>", Total_Medals, "</b> (Gold: ", Gold, " · Silver: ", Silver, " · Bronze: ", Bronze, ")<br>",
      "Medals per $100B GDP: <b>", Medals_Per_100B_GDP, "</b>"
    )
  )
```

## 1. Interactive Exploration: GDP vs. Unique Olympic Event Medals (1960–2016)

::: {.dashboard-card}
Does the size of a country's economy predict how many Olympic medals it wins? To investigate this question, I combined the Olympic dataset (`data/athlete_events.csv`) with real **World Bank Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** data in current US dollars (indicator **`NY.GDP.MKTP.CD`**). Because World Bank GDP records begin in **1960**, this exploration covers the **15 Summer Olympic Games from Rome 1960 to Rio 2016**.

Use the **Olympic Year dropdown menu** at the top-left of the chart below (or click items in the legend) to explore how the relationship between national GDP and unique Olympic event medals has evolved from **1960 to 2016**:

- **X-Axis (Log Scale):** National GDP in current US dollars (`$100M`, `$1B`, `$10B`, `$100B`, `$1T`, `$10T` · `NY.GDP.MKTP.CD`).
- **Y-Axis:** Unique Summer Olympic event medals won (`distinct(Year, Season, Games, Sport, Event, NOC, Medal)` so team sports count as one medal per event).
- **Hover over any country** to inspect its World Bank country name, Olympic `NOC`, `ISO3` code, exact GDP (`$ Billions`), total unique event medals (`Gold`, `Silver`, `Bronze`), and medals per `$100 Billion` of GDP.

```{r}
#| label: plotly-gdp-medals-by-year
#| fig-height: 6.5

# Prepare year-by-year traces so readers can switch cleanly across all 15 Summer Olympic years (1960–2016)
# or view 2016 immediately on load with full interactive hover details
summer_years <- sort(unique(summer_medals_by_noc$Year))
default_year <- 2016

group_colors <- c(
  "United States (USA)" = "#fbbf24",
  "Spain (ESP)" = "#ec4899",
  "Selected Europe (Other 11 Countries)" = "#a855f7",
  "Rest of World" = "#38bdf8"
)

fig <- plot_ly()

# Add 4 group traces per Olympic year (15 years * 4 groups = 60 traces)
for (yr in summer_years) {
  yr_data <- summer_medals_by_noc |> filter(Year == yr)
  is_vis <- (yr == default_year)
  
  for (grp in names(group_colors)) {
    grp_data <- yr_data |> filter(Group == grp)
    fig <- fig |>
      add_trace(
        data = grp_data,
        x = ~GDP_Billions,
        y = ~Total_Medals,
        type = "scatter",
        mode = "markers",
        name = grp,
        legendgroup = grp,
        showlegend = is_vis,
        visible = is_vis,
        text = ~Hover_Text,
        hoverinfo = "text",
        marker = list(
          size = ~pmax(9, pmin(26, sqrt(Total_Medals) * 2.6)),
          color = group_colors[[grp]],
          opacity = 0.88,
          line = list(color = "#0b1021", width = 1.2)
        )
      )
  }
}

# Build interactive dropdown items for each Summer Olympic year from 1960 to 2016
year_dropdown_buttons <- lapply(seq_along(summer_years), \(i) {
  yr <- summer_years[i]
  vis_vec <- rep(FALSE, length(summer_years) * 4)
  idx_start <- (i - 1) * 4 + 1
  vis_vec[idx_start:(idx_start + 3)] <- TRUE
  
  yr_rows <- summer_medals_by_noc |> filter(Year == yr)
  r_val <- round(cor(log10(yr_rows$GDP_Billions), log10(yr_rows$Total_Medals)), 2)
  
  list(
    method = "update",
    args = list(
      list(visible = vis_vec, showlegend = vis_vec),
      list(
        title = list(
          text = paste0(
            "World Bank GDP vs. Unique Summer Olympic Medals in ", yr,
            " (Log-Log r = ", r_val, " · ", nrow(yr_rows), " Matched Countries)"
          ),
          x = 0.01,
          y = 0.97,
          xanchor = "left",
          font = list(color = "#f8fafc", size = 15)
        )
      )
    ),
    label = paste0("Summer Olympics: ", yr)
  )
})

r_2016 <- round(
  cor(
    log10(summer_medals_by_noc$GDP_Billions[summer_medals_by_noc$Year == 2016]),
    log10(summer_medals_by_noc$Total_Medals[summer_medals_by_noc$Year == 2016])
  ),
  2
)
n_2016 <- sum(summer_medals_by_noc$Year == 2016)

fig |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = paste0(
        "World Bank GDP vs. Unique Summer Olympic Medals in 2016 (Log-Log r = ",
        r_2016, " · ", n_2016, " Matched Countries)"
      ),
      x = 0.01,
      y = 0.97,
      xanchor = "left",
      font = list(color = "#f8fafc", size = 15)
    ),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "National GDP in Current US Dollars (Log Scale · World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD)",
      type = "log",
      tickmode = "array",
      tickvals = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000),
      ticktext = c("$100M", "$1B", "$10B", "$100B", "$1T", "$10T"),
      gridcolor = "#2a3558",
      color = "#cbd5e1",
      tickfont = list(color = "#cbd5e1")
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Unique Summer Olympic Event Medals Won",
      gridcolor = "#2a3558",
      color = "#cbd5e1",
      tickfont = list(color = "#cbd5e1")
    ),
    paper_bgcolor = "#151c33",
    plot_bgcolor = "#151c33",
    font = list(color = "#f8fafc"),
    legend = list(
      orientation = "h",
      x = 0.27,
      y = 1.13,
      xanchor = "left",
      yanchor = "top",
      font = list(color = "#f8fafc", size = 11.5)
    ),
    updatemenus = list(
      list(
        type = "dropdown",
        direction = "down",
        x = 0.0,
        y = 1.14,
        xanchor = "left",
        yanchor = "top",
        active = length(summer_years) - 1,
        bgcolor = "#1d2642",
        bordercolor = "#a855f7",
        font = list(color = "#f8fafc", size = 12),
        buttons = year_dropdown_buttons
      )
    ),
    margin = list(t = 125, r = 30, b = 65, l = 65)
  )
```
:::

## 2. Why Country Matching & Limitations Matter: Correlation $\neq$ Causation

::: {.dashboard-card}
Linking international economic statistics to Olympic records requires careful country matching. Because International Olympic Committee (`NOC`) codes often differ from the World Bank's ISO-3166 alpha-3 (`iso3c`) codes, I mapped each modern `NOC` to its verified `iso3c` code and excluded dissolved or multi-state historical teams that cannot be matched to a single country's modern World Bank GDP series.

Crucially, **GDP is not direct sports investment**. World Bank indicator `NY.GDP.MKTP.CD` measures total national economic output across all goods and services—not athletic budgets, coaching systems, or community facilities. For instance, in **Rio 2016**, **Great Britain (`GBR`, GDP `$2.7T`, `67` medals)** and **India (`IND`, GDP `$2.3T`, `2` medals)** had comparable total GDP, yet very different Olympic outcomes. Neither total GDP nor elite sports funding alone explains this gap; Olympic medal totals reflect a complex mix of historical sporting traditions, grass-roots participation, per-capita income and public infrastructure, and which sports are included on the Olympic program (for example, cricket is India's most popular sport but was not contested in 1960–2016).

Finally, **correlation does not prove causation**. Although log-transformed GDP and log-transformed medal totals correlate strongly in 2016 (**$r = 0.72$** across **84 matched medal-winning countries**), a larger economy does not automatically cause Olympic victories. Total GDP is heavily confounded with population size, living standards, leisure time, and sports infrastructure, while countries such as **Jamaica (`JAM`, `11` medals with `$14.1B` GDP)**, **Kenya (`KEN`, `13` medals with `$74.8B` GDP)**, and **Cuba (`CUB`, `11` medals with `$91.4B` GDP)** regularly win far more medals than their GDP alone would predict through deep cultural specialization.

<details style="margin-top: 1rem; background: rgba(11, 16, 33, 0.55); border: 1px solid rgba(168, 85, 247, 0.35); border-radius: 10px; padding: 0.85rem 1.1rem;">
<summary style="cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600; color: #fbbf24;">Show Detailed NOC-to-ISO3 Country Matching & Excluded Historical Delegations</summary>
<div style="margin-top: 0.75rem; color: #cbd5e1; font-size: 0.95rem;">
- **Verified Code Translations:** Olympic NOC codes such as `GER` (Germany), `ESP` (Spain), `NED` (Netherlands), `SUI` (Switzerland), `GRE` (Greece), `POR` (Portugal), `DEN` (Denmark), `CRO` (Croatia), `SLO` (Slovenia), `RSA` (South Africa), `LIB` (Lebanon), `SIN` (Singapore), and `KOS` (Kosovo) are mapped explicitly to their ISO-3166 alpha-3 equivalents (`DEU`, `ESP`, `NLD`, `CHE`, `GRC`, `PRT`, `DNK`, `HRV`, `SVN`, `ZAF`, `LBN`, `SGP`, and `XKX`) using `countrycode` plus verified manual rules for pre-2016 IOC codes.
- **Excluded Historical & Multi-State Delegations:** To prevent silent mismatches, the following historical or non-sovereign Olympic delegations are excluded rather than forced onto modern single-country GDP series: **Soviet Union (`URS`)**, **East Germany (`GDR`)**, **West Germany (`FRG`)**, **Unified Team (`EUN`, 1992)**, **Czechoslovakia (`TCH`)**, **Yugoslavia (`YUG`)**, **Serbia and Montenegro (`SCG`)**, **United Arab Republic (`UAR`)**, **West Indies Federation (`WIF`)**, **Netherlands Antilles (`AHO`)**, **Individual Olympic Athletes (`IOA`)**, **Refugee Olympic Team (`ROT`)**, and the **1960–1964 United Team of Germany (`GER`)**, when East and West Germany competed together as a single combined delegation.
</div>
</details>
:::

## 3. Medals Relative to GDP: Top Medal-Winning Countries in Rio 2016

::: {.dashboard-card}
To view both **overall economic scale** and **medals relative to GDP** in the most recent Summer Games in our dataset (**Rio 2016**), the table below summarizes the top 15 medal-winning countries with verified World Bank GDP data, including **Spain (`ESP`)**. Note that `Medals per $100B GDP` is simply a descriptive ratio scaling medal counts by total economic size—not a measure of economic efficiency, since larger economies naturally exhibit diminishing returns under Olympic per-country entry caps:

```{r}
#| label: table-2016-gdp-medals

summer_medals_by_noc |>
  filter(Year == 2016) |>
  arrange(desc(Total_Medals), desc(Gold)) |>
  slice_head(n = 15) |>
  transmute(
    Country = paste0(country_wb, " (", NOC, ")"),
    ISO3 = iso3c,
    Group = as.character(Group),
    GDP_2016 = paste0("$", formatC(GDP_Billions, format = "f", digits = 1, big.mark = ","), "B"),
    Total_Medals = Total_Medals,
    Gold = Gold,
    Silver = Silver,
    Bronze = Bronze,
    Medals_Per_100B = Medals_Per_100B_GDP
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Country (NOC)",
      "ISO3",
      "Region Group",
      "2016 GDP (Current US$)",
      "Unique Medals",
      "Gold",
      "Silver",
      "Bronze",
      "Medals per $100B GDP"
    ),
    caption = "Top 15 Medal-Winning Countries at the 2016 Rio Summer Olympics Compared with World Bank GDP (NY.GDP.MKTP.CD)"
  )
```
:::
